title: Reverse sorting does not return ascending integers
claim: For every finite list of integers, the candidate returns the same integer values in nondecreasing order.

domain.description: All finite Python lists of integers, including empty lists; booleans are excluded from the domain.

property_description: The result contains exactly the input integers with multiplicities preserved, arranged in nondecreasing order. Empty lists are valid, and the input list is not mutated.
label_rationale: The candidate requests reverse order, so the input [1, 2] is returned as [2, 1], violating the nondecreasing-order part of the claim.

known_counterexample.reason: The output is descending rather than nondecreasing.
